subject: Temporary no-PO corridor proposal for TokenFlow ERP token vendor
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Khan <samir@tokenflow.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Temporary no-PO corridor proposal for TokenFlow ERP token vendor

Hi Laura, Aditya —

Quick one: TokenFlow (Samir copied) is standing up a short pilot integration for their API token billing tied to a 30-day trial. They need vendor setup and a billing route so they can invoice usage next month. Procurement timelines for a full PO + SOW look like 3–4 weeks, which would block the pilot.

I propose we grant a temporary no-PO corridor for TokenFlow for the duration of the 90-day pilot under the following guardrails:
- Spend cap: $2,000 / month max during the pilot
- Evidence: TokenFlow will provide SOC 2 (redacted), insurance, and KYC details before first invoice
- Accounting: Finance will set a special GL mapping and receive monthly usage reports
- Termination: Redwood can revoke the corridor with 5 days notice if anomalous billing observed

I'm attaching the vendor onboarding form and our redlines to their MSA so procurement/legal can review quickly. Can procurement evaluate and tell us what minimal checks you need to greenlight this temporary path? Samir, if you can share SOC2 and an initial invoice example that helps.

Thanks —
Irene
Irene Choi
Senior Product Manager, Platform
Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Temporary no-PO corridor proposal for TokenFlow ERP token vendor

Irene — thanks for flagging this. A few procurement items we need before we can move forward with a formal exception:

1) Evidence pack: SOC 2 Type II (or equivalent), Certificate of Insurance, business registration, and a primary contact for invoicing (email + PO if they later take one).
2) Risk assessment: product classification (is TokenFlow storing any Redwood customer data?), data processing agreement or confirmation that no customer PII will be stored.
3) GL mapping & payment terms: confirm who we bill to internally and whether we accept Net-30 for this vendor during pilot.

If those are provided, Procurement can approve a time-limited exception with the spend cap you suggested and with these controls: invoice-only intake, monthly reconciliation, and automatic conversion to PO when spend reaches 75% of cap.

Attaching the intake checklist I usually send to sales ops — fill the highlighted fields and return.

Laura Bennett
Procurement Manager
Redwood Inference
[attachment: procurement_checklist.xlsx]

Thanks — I support a limited exception to enable the integration, on these terms:
- Approve temporary no-PO corridor for up to 90 days, spend cap $2,000/month
- Require SOC2 evidence or completed security questionnaire before first billed invoice
- Finance to create a special cost center and we enable alerts at 60% and 90% of monthly cap
- Procurement to own the exception and confirm conversion steps to PO if we expect continued spend

Laura, can you prepare the formal exception memo (one page) and add the conversion trigger and monitoring owner? Procurement will sign off once Samir sends the SOC2 and KYC details.
